main_text.p: de Galien. Hoc autem affirmare verissimè mihi posse videor, in nulla vsquam Academia ita ve-ram vigere Medicinam atque in Parisiensi, à qua longè exulant Sophistice & Barbaries, quæ duæ pestes, sicut in alias omnes egregias disciplinas irruperant, ita in Medicina perditè sa-vicrant[?] apud superioris ætatis homines.

Apres le tesmoignage d'vn grand Medecin Professeur de Louuain, il n'y a plus de replique. Hieremias Thriuerius en l'Epistre & au commencement de son Liure de missione sanguinis in pleuritide, parle des Medecins de Paris de la sorte. Per Medicos Parisienses Medicinam plurimùm adiutam negare non possum, plurimáque quæ hactenus latuerant fateri debeo esse inuenta. Et au commencement de son Liure, il employe deux pages à la louange des Medecins de Paris, que ie rapporteray tout au long, pour faire voir que les Medecins de Paris sont les vrais restaurateurs de la Medecine.

VEHEMENTER ego vobis gratulari debeo, viri ornatissimi, vobis plurimum debet studiosa iuuentus, qui nescio an maiori labore, an fructu vberiore, Hippocratem & Galenum, duos Medicina antistites reuocastis. Hoc scio non minori negotio quàm Hercules Cerberum ad

page.notes: Large woodcut initial V of "VEHEMENTER" is set as a large letter; joined to the word. Italic and roman distinction in the lines above is read from the scan and may be imperfect. "sa-vicrant" (line-end hyphen after "sa-") is doubtful: the letters after the hyphen are not fully clear, hence [?]. Long s rendered as plain s throughout. Spelling "perditè", "verissimè" and "plurimùm" follow the printed forms as read.
